coverage.method: Every article's paragraphs, formula blocks, exercise prompt/answer, and takeaways were read individually. Explicit per-article notation mappings were applied and the converted mathematical contexts were reviewed; no automatic inference from a repository-wide regex was used.
coverage.protectedFields: Titles, summaries, references and reference notes, IDs, prerequisites, code, and all other structural fields were compared with the before snapshot and preserved.

checks: All 36 original section.formula fields converted to raw LaTeX without delimiters.
All 393 inline expressions parsed through mathSegments and renderMathText.
No protected content fields changed; all topic IDs and article ordering preserved.
Scanned prose outside explicit math delimiters for remaining Unicode operators, subscripts, exponents, and plain-text function/equation patterns.
Manually corrected a possessive boundary so paper's remains ordinary prose.

ambiguityDecisions.decision: Toy tokenizer symbols use upright text labels inside mathematical sequences; the SentencePiece whitespace marker remains literal text because it is a tokenizer character, not a mathematical variable.

BOS/A/B/EOS are upright token labels; N_batch and N_valid have textual subscripts. The existing valid-target sum is made explicit with a defined valid-position set, without changing which targets count.
Perplexity and named functions use operator notation. The existing sum over valid targets is preserved with an explicitly defined valid-position set.
A used as a matrix is typeset, while the English indefinite article A remains prose. This distinction was checked throughout LoRA articles.
Tensor shapes remain bracketed dimension lists; row-vector transpose conventions use a superscript T. Numeric parameter counts and break-even examples are unchanged.
Projection symbols Q/K/V/O are math; q_proj and other API identifiers remain literal prose. The target-sum index is written as j with textual input/output subscripts.
DoRA norms use paired norm delimiters, scalar/vector and matrix-axis qualifiers remain intact, and rsLoRA's square-root rank scaling remains distinct from standard alpha/r.
The existing selected-expert sum is expressed using a defined selected-expert set for token t.
The capacity factor is c, as already defined in prose; ceil is typeset with ceiling delimiters.
M is an upright million-parameter unit; the entire arithmetic expression is multiplied by M so both sides of the displayed inline equality use the same units, preserving counts 90M and 45M.
Convolution floor operations use paired floor delimiters; labels in the expanded prose equation remain upright text.
The original mean over masked-patch squared norms is expanded as a sum divided by the number of masked patches, with the masked set defined.
The positive key uses subscript +, candidate keys use subscript j, similarity uses operatorname, and temperature uses tau.
Preserved the distinction between per-pair sigmoid loss and the paper's batch-size reduction: B and B squared are typeset without altering the reviewed reduction claim.

Ordinary descriptive counts, model names, publication names, API identifiers, and prose method names remain text unless they are part of a mathematical expression, tensor shape, probability/parameter expression, or unit-bearing calculation. Titles and summaries are deliberately unchanged under the task scope.

scientificPreservation: This pass changes mathematical presentation, not objectives, assumptions, examples, numerical results, or reviewed reference claims. It does not constitute another scientific audit or model experiment.
